input.summary:
Windows, doors and porches is built: its two reported problems are fixed and make.sh gives a whole build.nbt (7293 cells, 394 placed, no OFF-PALETTE or REFUSED on this line).
The boarding-house sign was the off-palette spruce_hanging_sign. It is now a standing spruce_sign on the porch deck at (53,3,8), facing north, in a new porch_sign helper in parts/fittings.mjs.
Design change: the sign no longer hangs from the porch roof at y 5. Palette has no hanging or wall sign id, and the hanging spot had air under it, so it was the only palette-legal placement that is supported.

waste.what: Finding out which palette sign id could replace spruce_hanging_sign: I checked palette.json by hand, then ran mcd blocks --check, and worked out that the helper's hanging state cannot exist on the standing spruce_sign id.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and 1 reasoning pass
waste.tool: mcd blocks --check --palette palette.json <id> should print the nearest in-palette id and whether its shape (standing, wall, hanging) is available, so the swap is one command.

waste.what: Choosing a support-backed cell for the standing sign by hand (air above the deck, deck at y 2, no door or walk conflict).
waste.cost: about 3 cell checks by reading the porch layout
waste.tool: A palette-aware vocab helper, e.g. sign_on(g, text, x, y, z, {support: 'below'|'wall'}), that refuses unsupported cells and reports the nearest supported cell would have avoided the guesswork.

waste.what: Confirming the swap by re-running make.sh and reading the single part line, then reading the fittings source to make sure no other off-palette or refused writes remained.
waste.tool: ./make.sh --part 'Windows, doors and porches' (or a per-part report) would show only that part's line without the full 40-line log.
